title: Module Hierarchy
concept: Modules can be nested to create hierarchical namespace trees
why: Flat module structures don't scale. A library with 100 functions thrown into one module is as unmanageable as a 100-function file. Nesting creates logical trees (e.g., `net::http::client`) that mirror how engineers think about subsystems. It enables progressive disclosure — users drill into the depth they need.
theory: XIOM supports arbitrary module nesting. A module declared inside another forms a parent-child relationship accessed with `::`. The filesystem convention is: `mod math::geometry` maps to `math/geometry.xi` or `math/geometry/mod.xi`. The compiler builds a module tree at parse time. Child modules see parent `pub` items but not parent private items. Sibling modules are isolated from each other unless items are explicitly `pub`.
tips: Use `super::` to access the parent module from a child
Re-export deep items with `pub use` to flatten the public API
Keep nesting depth to 3-4 levels maximum
common_mistakes: Over-nesting — if modules have 1-2 items each, flatten them
Re-exporting without `pub` — the item stays private
